blocks.source: Vol IV, Deployment Release, § Safety Cases and Claims
blocks.md: A photograph of a clear aisle cannot establish that a loaded mobile base will stop before reaching an obstacle. A valid stopping claim depends on guaranteed physical clearance, actual braking capability, and end-to-end response timing, with each parameter supported by empirical evidence gathered under documented operating conditions. A safety case connects these physical premises to the release claim step by step, so an assessor can see which guarantees rest on measurements and which remain unverified assumptions.

questions.q: The section **Safety Cases and Claims** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A contained canary qualifies an update by a non-inferiority test on the intervention-rate ratio against a margin declared in advance, with sequential stopping.

Before signing, an independent reviewer hunts defeaters with probes at the envelope extremes, domain transfer, structural independence, and unmonitored wear, and the review recurs against normalization of deviance.
Fleet exposure narrows intervals for common outcomes but leaves rare severe outcomes wide, so each outcome's claim is licensed separately and disclosed.

Release adjudicates physical inequalities (stop inside the clear distance, contact force under the assessed limit, WCET inside its deadline) through a claim-argument-evidence case whose warrants say why each piece of evidence supports its claim.
